Subject: Pilot capacity ask for Sep ramp (MedSys POC)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our product team confirmed we need a short dedicated slice for the first two weeks of September to hit the latency and throughput objectives for the MedSys pilot. High level:~200 concurrent inference slots, 1.2M tokens/day expected during peak, and an aggressive SLA (p50 < 70ms) for the clinical triage endpoint.

Do you have a process for a temporary reservation + autoscale exemption? We’re willing to sign a short addendum and accelerate procurement if that helps. I attached our capacity request workbook with expected traffic patterns.

Questions we have:
- Minimum lead time you need to carve a dedicated pool for a pilot?
- Can we get an elevated autoscale threshold for two weeks (to avoid preemption)?
- Any additional networking/partitioning requirements for PHI?

If you want to loop infra, happy to do a quick sync this week.

Best,
Sophie Tran
Head of ML Ops, MedSys

Jordan / team —

Quick notes from procurement and pricing perspective:
- We can do a time-bound carveout (2 weeks) but we normally require a minimum prepayment or a short-term commitment to cover opportunity cost. For a pilot of this size I’d propose a one-month minimum at a reduced pilot rate; legal prefers to avoid one-off exceptions without at least minimal consideration.
- We’ll need the SOW to be explicit about the autoscale exemption window, the start/end dates, and rollback conditions.
- If PHI is in scope, we must route this through the Private offering (VPC) or ensure a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is attached; Ops needs confirmation from MedSys on data flows.

I can draft a small addendum and short SOW if we confirm the numbers and start date. Attachments suggested: proposed_reservation_sheet.csv and SOW_draft_medsys_v1.pdf.

One policy caveat: we reserve the right to throttle if cluster health drops below predetermined thresholds — the exemption isn’t absolute. We should be explicit in client communications.

—Kimberly

Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. Technical feasibility notes:
- 200 concurrent inference slots with p50 <70ms is achievable on a dedicated Tesla-class pool if we (a) pin the model to a quantized 4-bit variant and (b) enable prefix KV caching for their common request patterns. That reduces cost and helps latency.
- Autoscale exemption: we can carve a soft-reserve slab and raise the preemption threshold for the pilot window, but as Kimberly called out we must keep a fail-safe (cluster health + ops override).
- Lead time: give us ~3 weeks to provision and validate the pool and run a short stress test; that puts a provisioning cutoff in mid-August for a Sep 1 start.
- Runbook needs: a teardown checklist, an alerting playbook for latency/regression, and a shortlist of supported model configs. Laura — can you own the dashboard templates and the onboarding checklist?

I’ll prepare a brief tech appendix with recommended model configs and perf estimates and drop it in the Drive link.

-Marcus
VP, Serving Runtime
